error_kinds.meaning: An argument is missing, malformed or out of range.
error_kinds.fix: Check the call against the tool's input schema; the message names the argument.

error_kinds.meaning: No Space, run, window, service, tool or file with that id.
error_kinds.fix: List what exists first (list_spaces, agent_list, list_space_windows, list_tools).

error_kinds.meaning: The machine answered but runs no cua-spacesd, so the spacesd primitives cannot work.
error_kinds.fix: Use an image that runs cua-spacesd (for example ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04), or reach the Space's own services with list_tools and call_tool.

error_kinds.meaning: The Space's cua-spacesd reports a feature this tool needs as unsupported; the message names it and the driver's limitation.
error_kinds.fix: Use a Space whose spacesd supports the feature (see the tool's `requires`).

error_kinds.meaning: A prerequisite on this machine is missing: Fleet credentials, a local runtime, an operator display or app-session providers.
error_kinds.fix: Set up what the message names (see the tool's `host_requires`).

error_kinds.meaning: The operation does not apply to this kind of Space.
error_kinds.fix: Use a tool that serves the Space's provider (see the tool's `providers`).

error_kinds.meaning: The Space's spacesd or the cua.ai relay rejected the token.
error_kinds.fix: Re-add the Space with a valid token, or sign in again with `cua auth login`.

error_kinds.meaning: The signed-in account may not reach that relay machine.
error_kinds.fix: Sign in with the account that owns the machine.

error_kinds.meaning: The machine name given to on="host:<name>" fits several of your machines equally well; the message lists them.
error_kinds.fix: Ask the user which machine they meant, then pass on="host:<machine id>" from the list.

error_kinds.meaning: The host is at a capacity limit: two macOS VMs per Mac (Apple's macOS license, enforced by Apple Virtualization) or the host's own Space limit.
error_kinds.fix: Delete a Space on that host (delete_space), pick another machine, or create a Linux Space instead.

error_kinds.meaning: A short name matches more than one sandbox.
error_kinds.fix: Use the full id (`local:<name>` or `cloud:<name>`).

error_kinds.meaning: A file transfer did not land, or landed with a different sha256.
error_kinds.fix: Retry; check free space and permissions at the destination.

error_kinds.meaning: The teleport consent gate refused: a sensitive item without acknowledge_sensitive, a declined approval, or a Space that cannot import the app.
error_kinds.fix: Read teleport_manifest, then pass the items to move and acknowledge_sensitive=true for sensitive ones.

error_kinds.meaning: The Keyvault refused a site login: the user declined, no saved password matches the page's origin, the tab is on another origin, or the Keyvault is locked or off.
error_kinds.fix: Ask the user to approve the sign-in in Cua, import the site's saved password, or open the site's sign-in page and try again.

error_kinds.meaning: An agent run failed outside the transport: install, configuration or a refused message.
error_kinds.fix: Read agent_status and its output_tail for the reason.

error_kinds.meaning: A wait ran out: a claim that never bound, a Space that never became ready, or a command past its timeout.
error_kinds.fix: Retry, or raise the tool's timeout.

error_kinds.meaning: The create was cancelled (cancel_create, or its caller went away); what it made is gone.
error_kinds.fix: Nothing to clean up; create it again when you want it.

error_kinds.meaning: The media plane failed to open or run the stream.
error_kinds.fix: Check that the Space's spacesd supports desktop_stream or window_stream, then retry.

error_kinds.meaning: A cua-spacesd call failed.
error_kinds.fix: Retry; if it persists, check the spacesd log in the Space.

error_kinds.meaning: The Fleet control plane failed a cloud Space call.
error_kinds.fix: See the Fleet errors reference for the HTTP status in the message.

error_kinds.meaning: Fleet's admission refused the cloud Space: a size over this account's limits, or a template its policy does not admit. The message is Fleet's and names the limit.
error_kinds.fix: Pick a size within the limit the message names (most accounts run 1-8 vCPUs and 1-32 GiB), or contact Cua support to raise the account's limits.

error_kinds.meaning: The account is out of Cua Cloud credit (no credit left, and no card or plan): Fleet refused the new cloud Space. Running Spaces keep running; local Spaces are never affected. The message ends with the billing page's URL.
error_kinds.fix: Add credit on the billing page the message names (a plan, or a card for pay as you go), or create the Space locally.

error_kinds.meaning: The location, kind or runtime does not exist, or the combination (with the image) does not.
error_kinds.fix: Use one of the values the message lists, or leave kind and runtime unset (auto).

error_kinds.meaning: Starting, stopping or deleting the Space's sandbox failed.
error_kinds.fix: Check the local runtime (`cua doctor`) or the cloud pool, then retry.

error_kinds.meaning: Your cloud account refused or failed a call Cua made for a Space there (AWS, Google Cloud, Modal): a missing permission, a quota, a region without the instance type. The message names the cloud's own error.
error_kinds.fix: Fix what the message names in that account (`cua cloud test <provider>` checks without creating anything), or connect another region or project.

error_kinds.meaning: The cua.ai relay directory failed.
error_kinds.fix: Retry; check `cua auth status`.

error_kinds.meaning: An MCP service inside the Space failed.
error_kinds.fix: Check the service with list_tools; the message carries its error.

error_kinds.meaning: Reading or writing a local file failed.
error_kinds.fix: Check the path and its permissions on this machine.

error_kinds.meaning: A reply could not be parsed.
error_kinds.fix: Retry; report it if it persists.

error_kinds.meaning: The drive's access rules refuse this principal on this path (an agent outside its own home, its Space's folder, read-only public/ and its grants).
error_kinds.fix: Ask for access with volume_request_access; the user approves it in Cua.

error_kinds.meaning: A drive write or delete with if_etag or create_only found a different version at the path.
error_kinds.fix: Read the file again and retry with its current etag.

error_kinds.meaning: A write under agents/ carries something that looks like a secret (an API key, a token, a private key); it was not stored. The message names the kind and line, never the value.
error_kinds.fix: Remove the secret from the file; keep credentials in the Keyvault.

error_kinds.meaning: Another run holds the persistent agent's home (one writer at a time).
error_kinds.fix: Wait for that run to stop, or stop it; the lease expires on its own.

error_kinds.meaning: The user did not confirm with presence (Touch ID, the login password or the vault passphrase), so no access was widened.
error_kinds.fix: Ask the user to approve it in Cua.

error_kinds.meaning: The drive's store failed or is not configured (a bucket that refused, missing keys, or a backend this build cannot serve).
error_kinds.fix: Check `cua volume config show` and the message.

tools.name: add_space
tools.description: Add an existing machine as a Space by address and token.
tools.instructions: Tries a GetCapabilities handshake with the Space's cua-spacesd first. A local:<name> or cloud:<name> id without one is still a Space, with an empty capability set (its declared services, tunnels and public URLs work); a direct URL without one is added as an MCP Space when it answers MCP initialize (service `mcp`), and refused with spacesd_not_available when it answers neither. The Space is stored in ~/.cua/spaces.json and its token in ~/.cua/spaces-credentials.json (0600). Re-adding the same address updates it.

name.description: Display name. Default: the guest's hostname.

service.description:
For an MCP endpoint URL: the service name to register it under.
Default `mcp`.

token.description:
The spacesd token (or the bearer an MCP endpoint needs). Stored in
a separate 0600 credentials file, never in `spaces.json`.

url.description:
The Space's cua-spacesd: `http(s)://host:port` (port defaults to
3211), `host:port`, or a Space id (`cloud:<name>`, `local:<name>`).
Any other MCP endpoint (for example
`http://host:8765/mcp`) is added as a Space with one MCP service and
no spacesd capabilities.

tools.name: remove_space
tools.description: Forget a registered Space without touching it.
tools.instructions: Only the registration and its stored token are removed. The sandbox keeps running, including a Space in your cloud (its cloud resources and relay machine stay); delete_space deletes a Space that create_space made.
tools.result: JSON: `{"removed": <Space>}`, the registration that was removed.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: List the Spaces this connection can see.
tools.instructions: Every registered Space (cloud, local, direct and relay) with its id (local:<name>, cloud:<name>, direct:<host:port>, relay:<machine-id>), provider, spacesd version (empty without one) and supported features as of the last handshake. The signed-in account's machines on the relay are listed too: those are the names `create_space` accepts as on="host:<machine>". A Space a machine provides carries `host` (that machine's id) and `host_name`; group them under it when you show them. A Space in your cloud carries `cloud` (the provider: aws, gcp, modal), `cloud_place` (account and region, to show with it) and `cloud_delete` (where delete_space can delete it: here, host:<machine>, or elsewhere).
tools.result: JSON: an array of Spaces (`id`, `name`, `provider`, `spacesd_version`, `features`, `os`, `services`, `added_at`, for a Space one of your machines provides `host` and `host_name`, for a Space that can be turned off and on `power` (`suspend` or `stop`) and `power_state`, and for a Space in your cloud `cloud`, `cloud_place` and `cloud_delete`), each with `phase: "ready"`.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a Space: a new sandbox on this machine, on one of your machines, or in the cloud.
tools.instructions: Creates a new sandbox where `on` says (local: this machine, free; cloud: Cua cloud, metered; aws, gcp or modal: the user's own cloud account, connected with cloud_connect, billed there; default: the user's default location, else local), waits until it is ready (its spacesd when the image runs one, else its declared services), and registers it as local:<name> or cloud:<name>. `kind` (auto, container, vm) and `runtime` (auto, or an engine the location offers for the kind) are chosen automatically by default: the canonical Linux image runs as a gVisor container, macOS images as Lume VMs, Windows and disk-only images as VMs (QEMU locally, KubeVirt in the cloud). An impossible combination fails with invalid_placement and lists the valid values. Any image works; without cua-spacesd the capability set is empty. reuse=true returns a reachable registered Space in the same location with the requested services instead of creating one. On the user's own machines: on="host:<machine>" creates the Space on a machine set up with `cua host setup --provide-spaces` (for example "spin up 2 macOS Spaces on my spare Mac mini" is on="host:spare mac mini", image="macos", count=2). The machine is matched by id, exact name, or the words of its name; when several fit equally the call fails with ambiguous_host listing them (ask the user which, then pass on="host:<id>"). The host runs it with its own runtimes (Lume for macOS VMs on a Mac, Docker for Linux), the Space joins the relay and is returned as relay:<machine> with `host` set. A Mac runs at most two macOS VMs (Apple's macOS license, enforced by Apple Virtualization); a host at a limit fails with limit_exceeded. Only the machine's owner and the accounts it is shared with as editors can create there, from an enrolled device. on="direct:<addr>" is not accepted here: a direct address is one already-running Space, attached with add_space, not a host this call can create on.
notes: Cloud needs Fleet credentials (`cua auth login`); local needs a container engine, QEMU or Lume (`cua runtime doctor`).
tools.result: JSON: the registered Space, `phase: "ready"` and `reused` (true when `reuse` returned an existing Space); with `wait: false`, `{"id", "phase": "starting"}` at once; with `count` above 1, an array of them.

count.description:
How many Spaces to create, 1 to 8 (default 1), all with the same
settings (a name gets `-2`, `-3`, ... suffixes). With more than one
the result is an array.

image.description:
Guest image. Default: the canonical Linux image
(`ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04`), whose variant follows the kind.

kind.description: What kind of machine. Default `auto` (from the image).

oneOf.description:
From the image: macOS and Windows images are VMs, an image with a
container rootfs is a container, a disk-only image is a VM.
A virtual machine (QEMU or Lume locally, KubeVirt in the cloud).

on.description:
Where it runs: `local` (this machine, free), `cloud` (Cua cloud,
metered), or `host:<machine>`: one of the user's own machines that
provides Spaces (`cua host setup --provide-spaces` on it), named by
id or by words from its name ("host:spare mac mini" matches "Mac
mini (spare)" or `dillons-mac-mini`). Default: the user's default
location (`cua config set default.on`, `CUA_DEFAULT_ON`), else
`local`. Not `direct:<addr>`: that is one already-running Space at a
fixed address, attached with `add_space`, not a host this can create
on. An existing machine is added with `add_space`, not created.

reuse.description:
Return a reachable registered Space in the same location that has
the requested services instead of creating one (get-or-create).
Default false.

runtime.description:
Which engine. Default `auto`: the safest one for the location and
kind. Local: `gvisor` or `runc` (containers), `qemu` or `lume`
(VMs). Cloud: `gvisor` (containers), `kubevirt` (VMs). Anything
else fails with `invalid_placement`, listing the valid values.

services.description:
Named services (name to guest port), for example `{"mcp": 8765}`.
Each is probed for readiness and reachable with `list_tools` /
`call_tool` (`service=<name>`).

spacesd.description:
Whether the image runs cua-spacesd. Default: true for the canonical
images (and no image), false for any other image. A Space without it
has an empty capability set: only its services work.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for readiness (local). Default 600.

wait.description:
Wait until the Space is ready (its spacesd, or its declared
services). Default true.

tools.name: delete_space
tools.description: Delete a Space's sandbox and forget it.
tools.instructions: Deletes the sandbox of a Space that create_space made (cloud: metering stops; local: the instance is deleted; on one of your machines, on="host:...": that machine deletes it and it leaves the relay) and forgets it. A Space in your cloud (list_spaces: cloud, cloud_place, cloud_delete) is deleted permanently through the records of the device that created it: cloud_delete "here" deletes it from this device; "host:<machine>" asks that host (it must be online, and only its owner may); "elsewhere" is refused with where it was created: delete it there, or remove_space. Another Space added by address (direct:, relay:) is only forgotten: cua did not create it. Any hotspot on the Space is stopped first. To forget a Space without deleting anything, use remove_space.
tools.result: Text: what was deleted (`Deleted <id> (...)`), or `Removed <id> (...)` for a Space added by address.

tools.name: stop_space
tools.description: Turn a Space off: suspend it (memory kept) or stop it (disk kept).
tools.instructions: Turns a Space off the way its provider can: a local container or QEMU VM is suspended (its memory is kept and it resumes where it was), a local Lume VM is stopped (its disk is kept and it boots again), a Space one of your machines provides is stopped by that machine, which frees its memory, and a Space in your own cloud (on="aws", "gcp") is stopped there: compute billing stops, its disk stays (storage is still billed). Anything streaming from the Space and any hotspot on it end first. A Fleet cloud Space, a Modal sandbox, a Space added by address and your own computers on the relay cannot be turned off (wrong_provider); delete_space deletes a Space instead. start_space turns it on again.
notes: list_spaces says which Spaces turn off (`power`: `suspend` or `stop`; absent when it cannot) and how they were left (`power_state`).

tools.name: start_space
tools.description: Turn a Space back on: resume or boot it.
tools.instructions: Turns a Space stop_space turned off on again: resumes a suspended one, boots a stopped one (a Space one of your machines provides, or one in your cloud, joins the relay again), and leaves a running one as it is. Returns once it answers again (bounded). The same Spaces turn on as turn off.

tools.name: space_bash
tools.description: Run a shell command inside the Space.
tools.instructions: Runs through the spacesd's ProcessService with `/bin/sh -c`. Output is stdout, then `[stderr]` and stderr, then `[exit N]`; each stream keeps its last 16000 characters when longer.
tools.result: Text: stdout, then `[stderr]` and stderr, then `[exit N]`.

command.description: Command line, run with `/bin/sh -c` (`cmd.exe /C` on Windows guests).

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is killed. Default 60.

tools.name: space_write
tools.description: Write literal text to a path inside the Space.
tools.instructions: Written through FilesystemService, verified by sha256; no shell is involved, so nothing needs quoting.
notes: Literal text: no local file is read and nothing is shell-quoted, which is the whole reason it exists next to space_bash.
tools.result: Text: `wrote <path> (<n> bytes, sha256 <hex> verified in Space)`.

path.description: Absolute path in the Space. Parent directories are created.

tools.name: upload
tools.description: Send a local file or folder into the Space.
tools.instructions: Files stream through FilesystemService in chunks with a sha256 check; a folder is copied file by file (empty directories included, symlinks skipped). No size cap.
notes: Without `dest` nothing in the Space is replaced: a taken `<home>/<name>` lands as `<name> (1).ext`. An explicit `dest` is written as given and replaces a file already there.

dest.description:
Absolute destination path in the Space; an existing file there is
replaced. Default: `<guest home>/<name>`, or `<name> (1).ext` when
that is taken (nothing is replaced).

tools.name: send_file
tools.description: Send a host file or folder into the Space's Downloads, verified by sha256 on arrival.
tools.instructions:
The same transfer the Cua Spaces pop-out's Teleport drop zone performs: files land in the Space user's ~/Downloads through the spacesd's TeleportService (chunked, resumable, every file verified by sha256 before it is published). A transfer that does not land, or lands corrupted, is an error and not a reported success.

respect_ignorefiles (default true) applies ONLY when `path` is a folder. It honors `.gitignore` and `.ignore` at the folder root and in every subdirectory (each scoped to its own subtree, so a nested ignore file overrides its parent), plus `.dockerignore` at the root only. All three use gitignore semantics: negation (`!`), directory-only patterns (`foo/`), anchoring, `*`/`?`/`[...]`, `**`, comments, last-matching-rule-wins. As in git, an excluded directory is pruned and `!` cannot re-include anything beneath it. `.git/` is always skipped and symlinks are never followed. For a single named file it has NO effect.
notes: Unlike `upload`, the copy is verified in the Space by sha256 before the call returns: a transfer that does not land, or lands corrupted, is an error and not a reported success.
`respect_ignorefiles` applies only when the path is a folder, with gitignore semantics; a file named explicitly is always sent.
A file of the same name already in the Space is kept: the new copy lands as `name (1).ext` and its path is in `files`.

path.description: Host path (file or folder) to send.

respect_ignorefiles.description:
Honor `.gitignore` / `.ignore` (nested) and `.dockerignore` (root only)
when sending a folder. Default true. No effect on a single named file.

target_directory.description:
Subdirectory of the Space user's `~/Downloads` to land in. `~/Downloads`
and `~/Downloads/<sub>` are accepted too. Default: `~/Downloads` itself.

tools.name: download
tools.description: Fetch a file or folder out of the Space.
tools.instructions: Files stream through FilesystemService and are verified by sha256; a folder is copied recursively.
notes: Nothing on the host is overwritten: when `dest` already has an entry of that name the copy lands as `name (1).ext` (or `name (1)` for a folder), and `dest` in the result is the path used.

path.description: Absolute path in the Space (file or folder).

tools.name: stream_endpoint
tools.description: Return a ticketed media endpoint for the Space's desktop or one window.
tools.instructions: Opens a media session (StreamService.OpenMedia) for the desktop or one window and returns its ticketed WebSocket URL (rcdp wire v2, see libs/cua/proto/MEDIA.md). The ticket is short-lived, bound to that one session, and safe to put in a URL; it is not the Space's token. Works for every provider because the token comes from the SDK, not from the guest.
notes: Giving the caller frames is a different act from presenting the Space to an operator. FRICTION.md 10.
Replaces local_rcdp, which only worked for Local macOS Spaces and read its token over ssh.

app_name.description:
Stream the largest visible window of this app (case-insensitive
substring). Ignored when `window_id` is set.

display.description: Display id for a desktop stream. Default: the primary display.

ticket_ttl.description: Ticket lifetime in seconds (at most 600). Default 60.

window_id.description: Window handle from `list_space_windows`. Streams that window.

tools.name: list_space_windows
tools.description: List the windows open inside the Space.
tools.instructions: The windows a viewer can stream now, from StreamService.ListTargets: on screen, sized, normal app windows (no hidden, minimized or system-UI windows), each with its handle, title, app and bounds.

app_name.description: Only windows of this app (case-insensitive substring).

tools.name: stream_space_window
tools.description: Draw one Space window on the operator's desktop.
tools.instructions: FOR THE HUMAN. Opens a bidirectional window on the operator's desktop showing one Space window (the Cua Spaces app draws it from a media ticket). Pass app_name to auto-pick that app's largest visible window, or an exact window_id.
notes: Operator-side: the pixels land on the human's machine, so the platform axis is the operator's OS and not the Space's.

app_name.description: Auto-pick this app's largest visible window, e.g. "Firefox".

title.description: Label for the operator's window. Default: the window title.

tools.name: show_space_pip
tools.description: Pin the Space as picture-in-picture on the operator's desktop.
tools.instructions: FOR THE HUMAN, NOT FOR YOU. Pins an always-on-top picture-in-picture overlay of the Space onto the user's own desktop. Call it only when the user asks to see a Space; never to observe your own work.
tools.result: Text: `Pinned <space> as picture-in-picture on your desktop.`

tools.name: hide_space_pip
tools.description: Unpin the picture-in-picture window.

tools.name: open_space_viewer
tools.description: Open the full Space viewer on the operator's desktop.
tools.instructions: FOR THE HUMAN, NOT FOR YOU. Opens a live viewer window on the user's own desktop. Never call it to obtain a screenshot or to check on your own work; use the screenshot tool for that.
tools.result: Text: `Opened the <space> viewer on your desktop.`

tools.name: list_tools
tools.description: List the MCP services and tools reachable inside the Space.
tools.instructions: Lists the tools of an MCP service INSIDE the Space. `service` is any service the Space declares (an MCP server the image runs, reached over streamable HTTP; no spacesd needed) or `driver`, the spacesd's own cua-driver registry (screenshot, click, type, launch apps, accessibility, ...). The default is `driver`, or the only declared service of a Space without spacesd. With no `name`, returns a scannable overview; pass name=<substring> for full input schemas. Then invoke them with call_tool. The reply names every service the Space exposes.
tools.result: JSON: `service`, `count`, `tools` (`name` and `description`; with `name`, also `inputSchema`), `services`, `contract_version`, and a `hint` when no filter was given.

name.description: Substring filter; matching tools come back with full input schemas.

service.description:
Service. A service the Space declares (see `list_spaces`), reached
over generic MCP (streamable HTTP), or `driver` (the spacesd's
cua-driver registry; `mcp`, `cua-driver` and `computer-server` are
aliases unless the Space declares a service by that name). Default:
`driver`, or the only declared service of a Space without
spacesd.

tools.name: call_tool
tools.description: Call a service tool inside the Space.
tools.instructions: Returns the tool's content parts unchanged, images included. A tool-level failure comes back with isError, not as a transport error.
notes: Open world twice over: the callee is a tool the SDK has never seen.
tools.result: The called tool's own result, unchanged: its content parts (images included), `structuredContent` and `isError`.

arguments.description: Arguments object for the tool. Default `{}`.

service.description:
Service (see `list_tools`). Default: `driver`, or the only declared
service of a Space without spacesd.

tools.name: agent_start
tools.description: Start a coding agent in the Space.
tools.instructions: Installs the harness if needed (pinned, checksum-verified), gives it the Space's own MCP tools plus any mcp_servers, and runs it over the Agent Client Protocol as a detached spacesd process with auto-approved permissions (the Space is the sandbox). The run survives this server restarting or the connection dropping. Returns a run_id immediately: follow it with agent_events (cursor) or agent_status, continue it with agent_message, cancel a turn with agent_interrupt. Keys: env_from_host names provider key variables from this server's environment; host credential files are never copied.
notes: Runs auto-approved: the Space is the sandbox, which is why approvalsAreEnforced is false.

agent.description: Harness id. `agent_capabilities` lists what each needs.

base_url.description: A custom model endpoint base URL (a proxy or compatible server).

cwd.description: Working directory in the Space. Default: the run's own.

env.description:
More environment for the agent, for example
`{"HERMES_HOME": "/home/cua/bot"}`. Stored 0600 in the run and
redacted from its output; name provider keys in `env_from_host`
instead, so their values never pass through the conversation.

env_from_host.description:
Provider key variables to forward from this server's environment,
for example ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]. Names only; values never pass
through the conversation.

exit_when_idle.description: Stop (resumably) once the prompt is answered. Default false.

home.description:
Run as this persistent agent: its home in the Cua Volume
(`agents/<home>/`) is restored into the Space first and saved after
every turn, the harness keeps its memory there, and the agent gets
the `cua` bridge (notify_user, the drive). Creates the persistent
agent (this harness, this Space) when it does not exist yet. Default:
a one-off run whose state lives only in the Space.

mcp_servers.description: Extra MCP servers. The Space's own tools are always included.

items.description:
An MCP server for the run: `url` (streamable HTTP, reachable from inside
the Space) or `command` (stdio, run in the Space).

repo.description: Git URL cloned into the working directory first.

show.description:
Open a terminal on the Space's desktop following the run. Default
false.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Send a follow-up to an agent run.
tools.instructions: Continues the same session. While a turn runs the message is queued (or, with force=true, the turn is interrupted first); a run whose runner exited is restarted and resumes its session.

force.description: Interrupt a running turn first instead of queueing. Default false.

tools.name: agent_events
tools.description: Read an agent run's events after a cursor.
tools.instructions: Normalized events (install, session, turn_started, message, thought, tool_call, tool_update, plan, usage, permission, turn_ended, error, exited, ...) after `cursor`. Pass the returned cursor back to continue; caught_up=true means nothing more is written yet. The same kinds for every harness.
tools.result: JSON: `run_id`, `status`, `phase`, `events` (each `seq`, `ts_ms`, `turn`, `kind`, and `text`, `tool_id`, `tool_title`, `tool_kind`, `tool_status`, `stop_reason` when present; `category`: `message`, `user`, `activity` or `hidden`, and a one-line `summary` for activity; `raw` on request), `cursor` and `caught_up`.

cursor.description: `cursor` from the previous call. Default 0 (the start).

raw.description: Include each event's raw ACP payload. Default false.

tools.name: agent_status
tools.description: Read an agent run's status and result.
tools.instructions: status is running, idle, failed, crashed or unknown ('unknown' is never a guess). Includes the last turn's result (final text, stop reason, usage) and a rendered output tail. Read from files in the Space; never disturbs the run.

tail.description: Rendered output lines to return. Default 40.

tools.name: agent_interrupt
tools.description: Interrupt an agent run's current turn.
tools.instructions: Cancels the turn in flight (ACP session/cancel); the session stays open for agent_message.

tools.name: agent_stop
tools.description: Stop an agent run.
tools.instructions: Ends the run, then verifies its process is gone; reports stopped=false rather than claiming success.

tools.name: agent_list
tools.description: List agent runs in the Space.
tools.instructions: Every run in the Space, newest first, including runs another client started.

tools.name: agent_capabilities
tools.description: Report what the agent harnesses support.
tools.instructions: Every harness: readiness, what it installs, which key variables it reads, which endpoint wire formats it takes, and its known limits; plus the event kinds and statuses.

tools.name: persistent_agent_create
tools.description: Create a named agent whose memory outlives its Space.
tools.instructions: A persistent agent is a harness with a name, a Space and a home in the Cua Volume (agents/<name>/). Its harness keeps its memory in the home (Claude Code auto memory, Codex memories, Hermes MEMORY.md, the OpenClaw workspace), which is restored into the Space before each run and saved after each turn, so the agent remembers across runs, Space releases and machines. One run writes a home at a time. Start it with persistent_agent_send (or agent_start with home=<name>); the daemon notifies the user when a turn ends. Inside the Space the agent gets the `cua` bridge: notify_user, the drive, and the user's computers it was granted.

agent.description: Harness id. `agent_capabilities` lists what each needs.

base_url.description: A custom model endpoint base URL.

env.description: More environment for every run (not secrets; see `env_from_host`).

env_from_host.description:
Provider key variables forwarded from this server's environment at
every start, for example ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]. Names only.

name.description:
The agent's name: 1-63 of a-z, 0-9, `.`, `_`, `-`. Its home is
`agents/<name>/` in the Cua Volume.

space.description: The Space it works in (id or name).

tools.name: persistent_agent_list
tools.description: List persistent agents.
tools.instructions: Every persistent agent of this machine's cua home, with its Space, its current run and when its home was last saved.

tools.name: persistent_agent_remove
tools.description: Forget a persistent agent.
tools.instructions: Stops its run, removes its routines and forgets it. Its home (agents/<name>/) stays in the Cua Volume; delete it there.
tools.result: JSON: `removed` (the record). The home stays in the Cua Volume.

tools.name: persistent_agent_send
tools.description: Give a persistent agent a turn.
tools.instructions: A follow-up to the agent's idle run, or a new run with its home restored when it has none. Refused while a turn runs (never interrupts) and while paused. Follow the run with agent_events on the agent's Space.
tools.result: JSON: `run_id`, `started` (a new run, with the home restored) and `restored` (`files`, `bytes`, `millis`).

text.description: The message (the prompt of a new run, or a follow-up).

tools.name: persistent_agent_save
tools.description: Save a persistent agent's home now.
tools.instructions: Saves the agent's home from its Space into the Cua Volume now (the daemon also saves after every turn): only files whose SHA-256 changed move.
tools.result: JSON: `files`, `bytes`, `unchanged`, `removed`, `blocked` (files the secret scanner kept out) and `millis`.

tools.name: agent_pause
tools.description: Pause a persistent agent: its run, its routines and its Space.
tools.instructions: One call: stops the run, saves the home, releases the home's lease, keeps the agent's routines from firing, and suspends its Space when it is local. A cloud Space cannot be suspended (Fleet has no per-claim pause), so pausing releases it after the home is saved; agent_resume creates it again from the same image and restores the home. Apps open in a released cloud Space do not come back. The user's own machines are never suspended.

tools.name: agent_resume
tools.description: Resume a paused persistent agent.
tools.instructions: Resumes a suspended local Space, or creates a released cloud Space again from the same image, restores the home and lets routines fire again. With `prompt`, starts a run on it.
tools.result: JSON: `space` (it can change when a cloud Space is created again), `recreated`, `restored`, `run_id` and `ready_ms` (from the call to the home being back in a ready Space).

prompt.description:
Start a run on this prompt once the agent is back. Default: none
(the next message or routine starts one).

tools.name: routine_add
tools.description: Schedule a recurring turn for a persistent agent.
tools.instructions: Fired by `cua daemon` whether or not an app is open, as a turn of the agent (`[routine] <title>: <prompt>`). A routine never interrupts a turn: a busy or paused agent skips that slot. A daemon that was asleep fires a missed routine once on waking.

agent.description: The persistent agent that runs it.

prompt.description: What the agent is asked each time.

title.description: A short title (shown in the app and prefixed to the turn).

weekly_on.description: Every week at `<weekday> HH:MM` (local time), for example `mon 09:00`.

tools.name: routine_list
tools.description: List routines.
tools.instructions: Routines with their next firing and what the last one did.

agent.description: Only this persistent agent's routines. Default: all.

tools.name: routine_remove
tools.description: Delete a routine.

tools.name: routine_set_enabled
tools.description: Turn a routine on or off.

tools.name: notify_user
tools.description: Tell the user something in the Cua app.
tools.instructions: Posts a notification the Cua app shows ("Your research is ready"). Agents inside a Space get the same tool on their `cua` bridge.

agent.description: The persistent agent it is about, if any.

tools.name: notifications_list
tools.description: Read the notifications feed.
tools.instructions: The feed the Cua app turns into system notifications: turn ends of persistent agents, notify_user calls, access requests and failures. It persists while no app is open.
tools.result: JSON: `{"notifications"}`, newest first, each with `id`, `at_ms`, `agent`, `kind` (`turn_ended`, `message`, `approval`, `error`), `title`, `body`, `run_id`, `space` and `read`.

since_ms.description: Only ones newer than this (Unix ms).

tools.name: notifications_ack
tools.description: Mark notifications read.

ids.description: Ids to mark read. Default: every notification.

tools.name: computer_access_grant
tools.description: Let a persistent agent use one of the user's computers.
tools.instructions: Lets one persistent agent use one of the user's machines (its computer-use tools, through the agent's bridge). Asks the user for presence (Touch ID or passphrase) first. Other agents of the account get nothing.

expires_in_secs.description: End the grant after this many seconds. Default: until revoked.

machine.description:
The machine (a Space id, usually `relay:<machine-id>` from `cua
host setup`).

tools.name: computer_access_revoke
tools.description: Take back a persistent agent's access to a computer.
tools.instructions: Takes the access back at once: the agent's next call is refused. No presence needed.

tools.name: computer_access_list
tools.description: List per-agent computer access.
tools.instructions: Which agents may use which of the user's computers, and the audited record of grants, uses and refusals.
tools.result: JSON: `{"grants"}` (each `id`, `agent`, `machine`, `created_ms`, `expires_ms`, `revoked`) and, with `audit`, `audit` (newest first: `ts_ms`, `principal`, `action`, `path` (the machine), `detail`) plus `audit_verified`.

agent.description: Only this persistent agent's grants. Default: all.

audit.description: Include the audit log's newest entries (this many). Default 0.

tools.name: teleport_manifest
tools.description: Describe what a session teleport would move.
tools.instructions: Read on this machine from the app's own provider: items, sizes, which are sensitive and which are checked by default. With `space`, also reports whether the Space can import the app.
notes: The manifest is the thing an Approval is minted from: the SDK will not send a teleport the caller has not seen a manifest for.

space.description: Space to check the receiving side of (`GetManifest`). Optional.

tools.name: teleport_app
tools.description: Move an app session into the Space.
tools.instructions: Moves the app's signed-in session into the Space, but only through the Cua Keyvault and only with the user's consent. This tool never delivers on its own: the first call files a Keyvault access request and returns a request_id; the user approves it in Cua (Touch ID or the login password) or an unattended rule matches; a later call with the same request_id has the Keyvault broker perform the delivery over the daemon's authenticated channel. Without `include` the manifest's default-checked items move, never everything.
notes: Works on every provider. A comment in the SDK claiming teleport was cloud-only was stale and was a real bug: callers were being told to provision a metered Space for work a free Local Space does.

Consent is owned by the Keyvault broker, not this tool: the automation caller is treated as an unverified third party, so a delivery needs a live consent or an audited unattended rule and can never be self-approved (red-team E2).
tools.result: JSON. First call: `consent_required: true`, a `request_id`, `would_send` and `approve`. Retry with `request_id` once the user approved: `moved: true` with `transferred_paths` (what the Space imported), `import_ids` and `expires_ms`; or still `consent_required` while pending; or an `error` with the Keyvault code (`requires_cua_app`, `denied`, `disabled`) when it cannot proceed.

acknowledge_sensitive.description:
Must be true when the selection holds a sensitive item (credentials,
cookies). The consent is explicit rather than defaulted.

include.description:
Manifest `rel_path`s to send. Default: the manifest's default-checked
items, never everything. An empty list is refused as ambiguous.

request_id.description:
The Keyvault request id returned by a previous call. Present on a retry
after the user approved the teleport in Cua; the broker then performs
the delivery. Absent on the first call.

tools.name: request_site_login
tools.description: Sign in to a site in the Space with the user's saved password.
tools.instructions: Signs in to a website in the Space's browser with a password the user saved in the Cua Keyvault (imported from their browser). The first call files a Keyvault request and returns a request_id; the user approves it in Cua (Touch ID or the login password), once per sign-in by default. Call again with the same space, url and request_id: the Keyvault checks the page is on the saved login's exact origin, types the username and password through the Space's cua-driver, submits the form and returns what it did, never the password. Pass the browser tab you opened (session, target_id, tab_id from get_browser_state on the same Space) to sign in there; without one the Keyvault opens its own browser in the Space on `url` and returns its target_id and tab_id. `agent` names the persistent agent asking, shown to the user.
notes: The password never reaches the caller: the Keyvault fills the form through the Space's cua-driver and returns only a masked username.
Approval is required by default for every sign-in (one use per approval); only an unattended rule the user wrote skips it.
tools.result: JSON. First call: `status: "pending"`, a `request_id`, `site` and `space`. Retry with `request_id`: `status: "filled"` with `site`, `origin`, `username_hint` (masked), `submitted`, `page_url` and the browser `target_id`/`tab_id` it signed in; `status: "pending"` while the user decides; `status: "denied"` when they declined. Never the password.

agent.description: The persistent agent asking (shown to the user in the approval).

relay_plaintext_ack.description:
Sends the password over a relay connection that predates end-to-end
sealing even though the relay could read it in transit. Default
`false`: such a Space refuses the fill instead (S1).

request_id.description:
The request id a previous call returned. Present on the retry after
the user approved; absent on the first call.

session.description: cua-driver lifecycle session label of the browser tab to sign in.

url.description:
The site's sign-in page (http or https), for example
`https://github.com/login`.

username.description: Which saved username, when the site has several.

wait_secs.description:
Seconds to wait for the user's decision on a retry. Default 20, at
most 120.

tools.name: hotspot_start
tools.description: Start sharing this machine's network with a Space.
tools.instructions: Starts the Space's reverse-SOCKS hotspot (TunnelService.StartHotspot) and serves its egress from this machine, so the Space browses as this machine. Runs until hotspot_stop, delete_space, or this server exiting.
notes: Capability-gated rather than cloud-only: any Space whose spacesd supports `hotspot` can borrow this machine's network.

bypass.description:
Destinations (CIDRs or host suffixes) that keep using the Space's own
network.

set_system_proxy.description:
Point the Space's system proxy (and `HTTP(S)_PROXY` for new processes)
at the hotspot. Default true.

tools.name: hotspot_stop
tools.description: Stop sharing this machine's network.
tools.result: JSON: `{"stopped": [...]}`, the hotspots that were stopped.

space.description: Space id or name. Default: every Space with an active hotspot.

tools.name: hotspot_status
tools.description: Report which Spaces are sharing this machine's network, with counters.
tools.result: JSON: `{"hotspots": [...]}`, each shaped like hotspot_start's result.

space.description: Space id or name. Default: every Space with an active hotspot.

tools.name: volume_ls
tools.description: List a folder of the Cua Volume.
tools.instructions: Cua Volume is one versioned drive per account, shared by every Space and agent: public/ (shared reference, read by everyone), agents/<agent>/ (a persistent agent's home: memory, outputs, inbox) and spaces/<space>/ (per-Space scratch). As the user (the default) you see everything. With as_agent (and in_space) you see exactly what that agent sees: it reads public/, writes its own home and its Space's folder, and anything wider needs a grant the user approves.
tools.result: JSON: `path`, `principal` and `entries` (each `path`, `name`, `folder`, `size`, `modified_ms`, `etag`, `mode`, and `sync` when a file has something to say: `state` `pending_upload`, `conflict` (with `conflict_path`) or `conflict_copy`, and `written_by` when another device wrote it last).

as_agent.description:
See the drive as this persistent agent does (`ada`). Only narrows:
the agent's defaults and grants apply. Default: the user (the whole
drive).

in_space.description:
With `as_agent`: the Space id the agent is in, whose `spaces/<space>/`
folder it may write.

path.description: Folder, for example `agents/ada/` or `public/`. Default: the root.

tools.name: volume_read
tools.description: Read a file from the Cua Volume.
tools.instructions: Reads at most 8 MiB. Text comes back as utf8, anything else as base64.
tools.result: JSON: `path`, `size`, `etag`, `version`, `modified_ms`, `encoding` (`utf8` or `base64`), `content`, and `sync` while the drive's services run (`state` `synced`, `pending_upload`, `conflict` or `conflict_copy`; `written_by`, `conflict_path`).

version.description: A version id from `volume_history`. Default: the current version.

tools.name: volume_write
tools.description: Write a file to the Cua Volume.
tools.instructions: Every write is a new version (history is kept). if_etag makes it a compare-and-swap, create_only makes it create-only. Writes under agents/ are scanned for secrets and refused by kind and line; keep credentials in the Keyvault.

content.description: The content, as text or base64 (see `encoding`). At most 8 MiB.

create_only.description: Write only if nothing is at `path` yet. Default false.

if_etag.description:
Write only if the current version has this etag (from `volume_read`
or `volume_ls`): a compare-and-swap.

tools.name: volume_delete
tools.description: Delete a file from the Cua Volume.
tools.instructions: Adds a delete marker; volume_history and volume_restore still reach the old versions.

if_etag.description: Delete only if the current version has this etag.

tools.name: volume_history
tools.description: List a Cua Volume file's versions.

tools.name: volume_restore
tools.description: Restore an old version of a Cua Volume file.
tools.instructions: Writes the old version's content as a new version, so the restore itself can be undone.
tools.result: JSON: the new current version's `key`, `size`, `etag`, `version` and `modified_ms`.

tools.name: volume_grant
tools.description: Grant an agent or Space more Cua Volume access.
tools.instructions: Only for the user: widens an agent's or a Space's access past the defaults (an agent reads public/ and writes its own home and its Space's folder). The user confirms with presence (Touch ID, the login password or the vault passphrase) before anything widens; a grant that widens nothing is refused.

expires_in_secs.description: Lifetime in seconds. Default: until revoked.

note.description: A note shown next to the grant.

tools.name: volume_revoke
tools.description: Revoke a Cua Volume grant.

tools.name: volume_grants
tools.description: List Cua Volume grants.

all.description: Include expired and revoked grants. Default false.

tools.name: volume_request_access
tools.description: Ask the user for more Cua Volume access.
tools.instructions: Files a request the user sees in Cua; it grants nothing by itself. Poll volume_ls or volume_read to see when access arrives.

reason.description: Why (shown to the user as the agent's words).

tools.name: volume_requests
tools.description: List Cua Volume access requests waiting for the user.

tools.name: volume_approve
tools.description: Approve a Cua Volume access request.
tools.instructions: Only for the user, with presence.
tools.result: JSON: the grant the request became.

expires_in_secs.description: Lifetime in seconds. Default: until revoked.

tools.name: volume_deny
tools.description: Decline a Cua Volume access request.

tools.name: volume_audit
tools.description: Read the Cua Volume audit log.
tools.instructions: Every grant, revocation, request, refusal, blocked secret, sync, lease and agent access, from a hash-chained log; an edited or truncated log reports verified=false.
tools.result: JSON: `events` (each `seq`, `ts_ms`, `principal`, `action`, `path`, `detail`), newest first, and `verified` (with `error` when the hash chain does not verify).

tools.name: volume_storage
tools.description: Show where the Cua Volume keeps its bytes.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Keys are never returned; `has_keys` says whether the credential store holds them.

tools.name: volume_storage_set
tools.description: Test or change where the Cua Volume keeps its bytes.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Tests the storage first (bucket versioning, list, then write, read back and delete a probe object; retries path-style addressing to tell when a self-hosted store needs it); with dry_run nothing else happens. Otherwise, when the test passes, saves the setting and the keys (credential store) and switches the running drive to it without a restart. The bucket must have versioning on. cloud is refused.
tools.result: JSON: `ok`, `reachable`, `authorized`, `versioning`, `detail` (a sentence when not ok saying how to fix it), `problem` (`unreachable`, `bad_keys`, `forbidden`, `bucket_missing`, `versioning_off`, `path_style_needed`) and `applied` (saved and switched live).

access_key_id.description:
The access key id (with the secret; both or neither). Saved in the
credential store, never in a file.

backend.description:
`fs` (this machine) or `s3` (an S3-compatible bucket: AWS S3, R2,
MinIO). `cloud` is refused.

dry_run.description: Only test the connection; change nothing. Default false.

path_style.description: Path-style addressing (MinIO and most self-hosted stores).

root.description: A key prefix inside the bucket. Default none.

tools.name: volume_mount_status
tools.description: Show whether the Cua Volume is mounted as a volume.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. The drive can appear as a volume (Finder on macOS, a FUSE mount on Linux); it is off until the user turns it on with volume_mount.

tools.name: volume_mount
tools.description: Mount the Cua Volume as a volume.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Turns the mount on (kept across restarts) and mounts. Idempotent.
tools.result: JSON: the mount status after the attempt (see volume_mount_status).

tools.name: volume_unmount
tools.description: Unmount the Cua Volume volume.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Turns the mount off; files still uploading land first.
tools.result: JSON: the mount status after unmounting.

tools.name: volume_sync_status
tools.description: Show the Cua Volume's sync state across devices.
tools.instructions: Devices sharing one bucket learn each other's changes through a change log in the bucket itself. A write that lost to a later one is never dropped: it stays in the file's history and as the visible conflict copy. A persistent agent may call it too (through its bridge): it sees the pending uploads and conflicts of files it can read and its own Space's volume. In a Space it reports this machine's view.
tools.result: JSON: `device_id`, `device_name`, `feed` (`live`, `off` for a store on this machine, `offline` when the bucket stops answering, with `last_error`), `poll_interval_ms`, `last_poll_ms`, `last_remote_change_ms`, `pending_uploads`, `pending_bytes`, `conflicts` (each `path`, `conflict_path`, `winner_device`, `loser_device`, `winner_version`, `loser_version`, `ts_ms`), `devices` (each `id`, `name`, `this_device`, `last_seen_ms`, `last_change_ms`, `changes`), `last_error`, `pending` (each `path`, `bytes`: files still uploading), `backend` (`fs` or `s3`), `mount` (this machine's mount: `off`, `mounting`, `mounted`, `needs_approval`, `unsupported`, `error`), `cache` (a bucket's block cache, when there is one) and `volumes` (the volume mounted in Spaces: each `space`, `mount_path`, `backend`, `principal`).

tools.name: volume_sync_events
tools.description: Wait for Cua Volume sync events.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. A long poll: answers at once when events newer than since_seq exist, else waits up to wait_ms for one. Kinds: remote_change, remote_delete, upload_started, upload_done, upload_failed, conflict, error.

since_seq.description: Return events after this `seq` (default 0: all kept).

wait_ms.description:
Wait up to this long for one when none is newer (default 0, at most
30000).

tools.name: volume_sync_resolve
tools.description: Mark a Cua Volume sync conflict as seen.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Clears the conflict from the list; both files stay.

tools.name: volume_cache_stats
tools.description: Show the Cua Volume block cache.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Reads of a remote store go through a local block cache; counters are since the runtime started.

tools.name: volume_cache_set
tools.description: Set the Cua Volume block cache's size cap.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Evicts down to the new cap at once; kept across restarts.
tools.result: JSON: the cache stats after the change.

tools.name: volume_cache_clear
tools.description: Clear the Cua Volume block cache.
tools.instructions: Only for the user. Drops every cached block; files stay in the drive.
tools.result: JSON: the cache stats after clearing.

tools.name: share_space
tools.description: Let another cua.ai account watch or edit a Space.
tools.instructions: Shares the Space through the cua.ai relay with one account, by verified email or account id; the same allowlist and device enrollment `cua host share` uses. A viewer joins presence with their own named cursor and watches a view-only stream: the Space's driver refuses their input, shell, files and MCP. An editor gets full use, and their input is a human session. Sharing again changes the role. A host (`relay:<id>`) is shared directly; any other Space (local, cloud, or added by address) is attached to the relay on its first share: its own driver dials out, so it needs no inbound port. Invitees open `invitee_space`.
notes: Viewers and editors are enforced by the Space's own cua-spacesd, not by the caller; a Space whose driver predates relay_attach reports capability_missing.
tools.result: JSON: `space`, `machine` (the relay machine it is shared as; empty when not shared), `invitee_space` (what the people it is shared with open: `relay:<machine>`), `url`, `online` and `shares` (each `who`, `role`: viewer or editor, and `connected`).

role.description:
`viewer` (presence with their own cursor and a view-only stream) or
`editor` (full use; their input is a human session). Default
`viewer`.

who.description:
Who: an email address (verified by cua.ai) or an account id. Teams
are not accepted: share with each member.

tools.name: unshare_space
tools.description: Stop sharing a Space with an account, or with everyone.
tools.instructions: Removes one account (or everyone) at once: the relay cuts their open streams and refuses new calls. With no `who`, the Space stops being shared and a Space that is not a host leaves the relay.
tools.result: JSON: `space`, `machine` (the relay machine it is shared as; empty when not shared), `invitee_space` (what the people it is shared with open: `relay:<machine>`), `url`, `online` and `shares` (each `who`, `role`: viewer or editor, and `connected`).

who.description:
The email or account id to remove. Default: everyone (the Space
stops being shared; a Space that is not a host leaves the relay).

tools.name: space_shares
tools.description: List who a Space is shared with.
tools.instructions: Who the Space is shared with, in which role, and who of them is connected through the relay now.
tools.result: JSON: the shares (see share_space) and, with `audit`, `audit`: the newest owner-side lines (`ts_ms`, `action`: share, unshare, attach or detach, `space`, `detail`).

audit.description:
Also return this many of the newest owner-side audit lines. Default
0.

tools.name: relay_register_space
tools.description: Publish a Space on the relay for the account's other devices.
tools.instructions: Publishes the Space as a machine of the signed-in account on the cua.ai relay, the way `cua host setup` publishes this computer: the Space's own driver joins the relay over outbound WSS with a machine token the account registered, so no inbound port is opened. The account's other devices (a phone off this network, the Cua app on another computer) then open `relay_space`; nobody else can until share_space adds them. Idempotent, and it re-attaches a Space that restarted. Needs a driver with relay_attach (a host is already registered).
tools.result: JSON: `space`, `relay_space` (`relay:<machine>`: how the account's other devices reach it), `machine`, `url` and `online`.

tools.name: relay_unregister_space
tools.description: Take a Space off the relay.
tools.instructions: Takes the Space off the relay: its driver leaves and its machine is removed, with every share. A host is removed with `cua host remove` on that machine instead.
tools.result: JSON: `space` and `unregistered` (false when it was not on the relay).

tools.name: cloud_status
tools.description: List your clouds (AWS, Google Cloud, Modal): found credentials, the connected account and region, what each can run at what hourly cost, and what Cua created there.
tools.instructions: Sandboxes and Spaces can run in the user's own cloud account: on="aws" (EC2), "gcp" (Compute Engine) or "modal" (Modal Sandboxes). EC2 and Compute Engine start one small VM per sandbox that runs the image with Docker; Modal runs one Modal sandbox. Either way the guest's cua-spacesd dials out to the cua.ai relay as a machine of the signed-in account (no inbound port), and the Space is that machine, relay:<machine>. Each cloud uses its own CLI sign-in; connect it first with cloud_connect (the user decides; it costs money in their account). Everything Cua creates is tagged cua-managed=true with this cua home's cua-owner and an expiry, recorded under the cua home, deleted with its sandbox, and ends itself at its expiry; cloud_sweep removes leftovers.
tools.result: JSON: `default_on`, `providers` (each `name`, `title`, `tier` (`vm`: a VM that provides Spaces, `sandbox`: one sandbox per Space), `connected`, `default`, `credentials` (`found`, `source`), `account`, `profile`, `region`, `zone`, `project`, `environment`, `label` ("AWS · us-west-2"), `ttl_hours` and `kinds` (each `image`, `kind`, `supported`, `reason`, `machine_type`, `usd_per_hour`)) and `resources` (what Cua created: `provider`, `id`, `type`, `space`, `region`, `state`, `created`, `expires`, `expired`).

provider.description: Only this cloud (`aws`, `gcp`, `modal`). Default: every one.

tools.name: cloud_connect
tools.description: Connect a cloud account Spaces can be created in.
tools.instructions: Runs cloud_test first and connects only when every check passes. Stores the profile, region, project or environment names under the cua home (never a key: the cloud's own CLI sign-in stays where it is). With make_default, create_space without `on` creates there (`default.on`).
tools.result: JSON: the connected cloud as `cloud_status` lists it, plus `checks` (each `name`, `ok`, `detail`) from the test it ran first.

make_default.description: Also make it the default location (`default.on`). Default false.

profile.description:
AWS: the profile in `~/.aws/config` (default: `default`, or
`AWS_PROFILE`). Modal: the profile in `~/.modal.toml` (default: the
active one).

project.description: GCP project id (default: `gcloud config get project`).

region.description:
AWS region (default: the profile's, else `us-west-2`) or GCP region
(default `us-central1`).

ttl_hours.description:
Every Space created there deletes itself after this many hours
(the instance or sandbox terminates, the sweeper removes what is
left). Default 8; 0 keeps Spaces until you delete them (Modal caps
a sandbox at 24).

zone.description: GCP zone in the region (default: its `-a` zone).

tools.name: cloud_test
tools.description: Check a cloud account without creating anything.
tools.instructions: Creates nothing: it signs in with the cloud's own CLI credentials, asks the cloud to validate a create without doing it (AWS DryRun, Google Cloud permission checks), and reads quotas. A failed check says what to fix.
tools.result: JSON: `provider`, `ok`, `account` (the account, project or workspace the credentials reach) and `checks` (each `name`, `ok`, `detail`: credentials, permissions by dry run, quota, the region and machine types).

profile.description:
AWS: the profile in `~/.aws/config` (default: `default`, or
`AWS_PROFILE`). Modal: the profile in `~/.modal.toml` (default: the
active one).

project.description: GCP project id (default: `gcloud config get project`).

region.description:
AWS region (default: the profile's, else `us-west-2`) or GCP region
(default `us-central1`).

zone.description: GCP zone in the region (default: its `-a` zone).

tools.name: cloud_disconnect
tools.description: Forget a connected cloud account.
tools.instructions: Forgets the connection (and `default.on` when it named this cloud). Nothing in the cloud is deleted.
tools.result: JSON: `provider`, `disconnected` and `left` (resources Cua still records there; delete their Spaces, or cloud_sweep with all=true, to remove them).

tools.name: cloud_sweep
tools.description: Find and delete what Cua left in your clouds.
tools.instructions: Acts only on resources that carry Cua's tags (cua-managed=true and this device's cua-owner) and that this cua home recorded, or that carry this device's owner id: never on anything else in the account. Default dry_run=true lists what it would delete: expired Spaces (past their ttl), resources whose Space is gone, and with all=true every Cua resource there.

all.description:
Also delete Cua resources that have not expired yet (every Space
in that cloud). Default false: only expired ones, and resources no
Space refers to any more.

dry_run.description: List what would be deleted without deleting it. Default true.

provider.description: Only this cloud. Default: every connected one.
